svg.title: The three boot classifications at the boot gate
svg.desc: Sequence diagram of the three starts. Clean start: a FLUSHED quorum vouches, one round writes RUNNING, the process reads its era and re-syncs in-cluster. Controlled halt then clean start: two rounds down, one round up. Dirty fast start: no FLUSHED quorum; the bumped identity pair is flushed before any emission — the identity law — and the process then gossips, catches up, rejoins, writing the deferred RUNNING latch only after the rejoin.
svg.text: The boot gate: three starts, three write schedules
One question from durable state — did the previous process reach its drain point? — chooses the path.
process
superblock quorum (4)
cluster
1. Controlled halt — two rounds
round 1: 4× STOPPED (read loop halted, handlers drained)
the dual-ring WAL is forced to stable storage
round 2: 4× FLUSHED — vouches for everything beneath; exit
2. Clean start — one round
read quorum: FLUSHED — the state beneath is vouched
one round: 4× RUNNING (the latch), before the first message
read the era from the vouched state; re-sync in-cluster — a partition heal, not a crash
3. Dirty fast start — no round now, one round later
read quorum: no FLUSHED — crashed; uninitialised; time is of the essence
the identity gate: increment {systemIdentifier, crashCounter}, 4× commit — before any emission
rejoin gossip to every known node, carrying frontiers
the leader streams from the frontier, then a fresh commit; catch up, rejoin
deferred: 4× RUNNING — the latch is written only after the rejoin
a second crash before the deferred latch still reads no FLUSHED quorum — crashed again, and the counter increments again
the state flush is never paid at the boundary; the identity flush always is (§5)
